name: FloodRoot
description: An explicit scope for the neutral dark foundations profile.
notes: Import @flood-md/react/styles.css once at the application entry.
This root selects neutral/dark locally. Legacy controls outside it keep their earlier theme behavior.

name: Text
description: Role-based interface text, from introductory copy to small supporting details.
code:
<Stack gap="3">
  <Text as="p" size="lead">Quarterly revenue</Text>
  <Text as="p" size="compact">Revenue increased by 8% this quarter.</Text>
</Stack>
notes: Use as="p" for paragraphs. The label size does not create a form association.
Subtle is a supplementary tone; evaluate small required instructions against the actual background and font size.

name: Heading
description: Semantic heading levels with an independent visual scale.
code:
<Stack gap="4">
  <Heading level={2} size="page">Workspace settings</Heading>
  <Heading level={3} size="section">Notifications</Heading>
</Stack>
notes: Choose level for document structure and size for appearance.
Display is a large marketing role. Keep page and section sizes for ordinary product interfaces.

name: Stack
description: Vertical composition with spacing from the shared token scale.
code:
<Stack gap="4">
  <Heading size="section">Project</Heading>
  <Text as="p">One place for your work.</Text>
</Stack>
notes: The parent owns the gap between its children.
Spacing keys are strings and use rem. Flood does not reset the host root font size.

name: Inline
description: A wrapping horizontal group for related content and actions.
notes: Inline wraps when its children need more space.
Use the same control size for neighboring actions of the same level.
Rows center items by default. Use gap="4" between independent choices; gap="2" remains available for tightly related content.

name: Surface
description: A quiet container with semantic elevation and token-based padding.
notes: Elevation describes appearance. Overlay does not create a dialog, portal or focus trap.
Prefer grouping and spacing before adding more nested containers.

name: Divider
description: A semantic separator with a low-emphasis visual line.
notes: The line is decorative in contrast terms: content grouping must remain understandable without seeing it.
Divider renders a native hr; it has no orientation prop.

name: Button
description: Native actions with a clear prominence, size and interaction state.
notes: Button defaults to type="button". Set submit or reset deliberately inside forms.
Loading disables activation and sets aria-busy. The host owns completion announcements.
Prefer subtle for standalone secondary actions; ghost belongs in a clear parent context.
Buttons use content width, including inside Stack. Opt into a full-width action with style={{ inlineSize: "100%" }} only when the composition calls for it.

name: IconButton
description: An icon-only action with a required accessible name.
notes: Provide a meaningful action label, rather than the name of the glyph.
Supply a licensed SVG. IconButton wraps it in a decorative IconSlot sized to the control.
Connect onClick to your host action. The interactive preview adds a local count; the basic usage snippet only shows composition.

name: Link
description: A native anchor for navigation.
notes: Use a button for state-changing actions and a link for navigation.
Link forwards native anchor attributes. Its optional solid/subtle/outline/ghost variants share Flood Button geometry; text is the unchanged default. No asChild API.

name: Field
description: The association between a visible label, its input and supporting messages.
code:
<Field label="Project name" required hint="Visible to your team.">
  {(control) => <Input {...control} name="project" />}
</Field>
notes: Spread the supplied control props onto one Input or Textarea.
Field merges describedBy with hint/error IDs and forwards native required through its function child.
The host owns validation rules. Compose Field in a client component in Next.js.
Field is not a generic native div wrapper and does not forward a ref.

name: Input
description: A native input with semantic styling and independent visual sizing.
notes: Use Field or a native associated label; placeholder text is not a label.
controlSize changes appearance. The native numeric size attribute keeps its HTML meaning.
Default outlines use the quiet field.border role. field.boundary is a stronger opt-in; preserve the independent focus indicator when customizing colors.

name: Select
description: A Flood choice field with its own popup and native form integration.
notes: Single selection uses a Flood trigger and listbox, including the popup. Native options and optgroups supply the choices; disabled choices cannot be selected.
Use arrows, Home/End and typing to navigate; Enter or Space confirms, Escape cancels. The popup scrolls active choices into view.
Select fills its Field; constrain the form or field wrapper. Multiple and numeric size greater than one use a native inline listbox rather than a popup.
A native form bridge preserves name, value/defaultValue, required, disabled, onChange and HTMLSelectElement ref. Inspect the matching guide for the visible focus contract.

name: Textarea
description: Native multiline input for notes and longer text.
code:
<Field label="Project note" hint="Keep it short and useful.">
  {(control) => <Textarea {...control} rows={3} maxLength={500} />}
</Field>
notes: Rows, maxLength, value/defaultValue and form props remain native.
The default has no resize grip. Long text scrolls inside the field; a host can opt into native resizing with style={{ resize: "vertical" }}.

name: Checkbox
description: A labeled native checkbox for independent choices.
notes: Use checked/onChange for controlled state or defaultChecked for native state.
Labels stay visible. Disabled does not mean read-only; explain unavailable choices outside the disabled control when needed.

The control and visible label form one content-width unit with an 8px-at-16px-root internal gap. Use an explicit parent gap="4" (16px at that root) between units; the glyph keeps its token-defined size.
indeterminate sets the native mixed state after hydration; checked still controls form submission. The host owns select-all aggregation and updates. Radio and Switch do not expose this prop.

name: Radio
description: A labeled native radio for one choice within a group.
code:
<fieldset>
  <legend>Visibility</legend>
  <Radio label="Private" name="visibility" value="private" defaultChecked />
  <Radio label="Public" name="visibility" value="public" />
</fieldset>
notes: Radios in one group share a name. The host supplies fieldset and legend.
Native browser keyboard and form behavior remain available.

The control and visible label form one content-width unit with an 8px-at-16px-root internal gap. Use an explicit parent gap="4" (16px at that root) between units; the glyph keeps its token-defined size.

name: Switch
description: A labeled on/off setting with native checkbox form behavior.
notes: Switch uses a native checkbox with role="switch".
checked/defaultChecked, name/value, reset and disabled remain native. The component does not persist settings.

The control and visible label form one content-width unit with an 8px-at-16px-root internal gap. Use an explicit parent gap="4" (16px at that root) between units; the glyph keeps its token-defined size.

name: CodeSnippet
description: Selectable, wrapping code with an optional host-owned action.
notes: CodeSnippet escapes code content and uses the semantic system monospace font stack.
The host implements copy behavior, failure handling and feedback. No clipboard or network API runs inside the component.
Code text defaults to LTR independently of parent layout. codeDirection can be ltr/rtl/auto; native dir still controls the wrapper and action layout.

name: IconSlot
description: Consistent geometry for a host-supplied SVG icon.
notes: No glyph pack ships in the React package. Keep the license of the host's icon artwork.
Without label the slot is decorative. With label it exposes role="img" and an accessible name.
Use an SVG rather than a text character. Avoid inline SVG sizing styles that override the slot.

name: ScrollArea
description: Native scrolling with inset overlay scrollbars that preserve content width.
code:
<ScrollArea aria-label="Recent activity" style={{ maxHeight: "12rem" }}>
  <Stack gap="4">
    <Text>Project created.</Text>
    <Text>Workspace updated.</Text>
  </Stack>
</ScrollArea>
notes: Scrollbars overlay the viewport with an inset; they do not reserve a content gutter. Give the viewport an explicit height or maxHeight to produce vertical overflow.
The forwarded ref, className, style and native div props belong to the scrollable viewport. Supply a visible context or accessible label for keyboard users.

Wheel, touch and keyboard scrolling remain native. Default contentInset="scrollbar" keeps text and full-width rows clear of rails with inner padding, without shrinking the viewport. Explicit none allows edge-to-edge content when the host already provides safe padding. Rails automatically avoid rounded clipping corners.
Forced colors restores native scrollbars as an accessibility fallback. Verify horizontal and RTL content, resizing and zoom in the host composition.

name: Label
description: A native label that connects a visible name to a control.
code:
<Stack gap="2">
  <Label htmlFor="project-label">Project name</Label>
  <Input id="project-label" defaultValue="My project" />
</Stack>
notes: htmlFor connects the label to a matching control ID; implicit nested controls also retain native behavior.
required adds a decorative marker only. Set required on the actual control as well. Field already composes Label.

name: Fieldset
description: A native group with a legend, shared descriptions and disabled form behavior.
code:
<Fieldset legend="Notifications" hint="Choose the updates you want.">
  <Checkbox label="Product updates" name="updates" defaultChecked />
  <Checkbox label="Release notes" name="releases" />
</Fieldset>
notes: Uses a real fieldset and legend, with a ref to HTMLFieldSetElement. Disabled descendants retain native form semantics.
The browser exempts controls in the first legend from inherited disabling. Avoid interactive legend contents unless this is intentional.
hint, message, error and external aria-describedby IDs are merged without duplicates. Error takes precedence over an advisory status.
Group status describes the group; it does not mark every child invalid, manage selected values or implement a RadioGroup/CheckboxGroup.

legendSize="section" gives an independent form section a 1rem semibold title and a 1rem body inset. The default "label" remains a compact choice caption; neither option changes native group semantics.

name: RadioGroup
description: A named single-choice group with native radio keyboard and form behavior.
code: <RadioGroup name="visibility" legend="Visibility" options={[{ value: "private", label: "Private" }, { value: "team", label: "Team" }]} defaultValue="private" />
notes: Composes Fieldset and existing native choice controls. The ref targets HTMLFieldSetElement; options need unique values and visible labels.

value/onValueChange is controlled; defaultValue initializes an uncontrolled group. Native form reset restores uncontrolled defaults without firing onValueChange; controlled values remain owned by the host.
name belongs to the inputs. The form prop associates every input with an external form. Disabled options and groups follow native submission rules.
RadioGroup supports native required. CheckboxGroup returns repeated name/value entries; validate minimum/maximum selections in the host and explain errors through status/message.

name: CheckboxGroup
description: A named multiple-choice group with a shared array value and native form behavior.
code: <CheckboxGroup name="notifications" legend="Notifications" options={[{ value: "updates", label: "Product updates" }, { value: "releases", label: "Release notes" }]} defaultValue={["updates"]} />
notes: Composes Fieldset and existing native choice controls. The ref targets HTMLFieldSetElement; options need unique values and visible labels.

value/onValueChange is controlled; defaultValue initializes an uncontrolled group. Native form reset restores uncontrolled defaults without firing onValueChange; controlled values remain owned by the host.
name belongs to the inputs. The form prop associates every input with an external form. Disabled options and groups follow native submission rules.
CheckboxGroup has no required/min/max shortcut: a required checkbox means that specific checkbox. Validate the selected array in the host and use group status/message.

name: ButtonGroup
description: Connected actions with shared edges and ordinary keyboard focus.
notes: Use direct Button/IconButton children with compatible sizes. The group owns connected radii and single separators; actions keep their props and handlers.
label names the group. Tab follows normal button order; this is not a toolbar, menu or selection group.
Horizontal is default; vertical stacks actions. Content can wrap within a button. Conditional/hidden actions preserve the visible end corners. No clipping masks focus.

name: InputGroup
description: One native text input with logical start/end content inside a shared perimeter.
notes: Ref, id, name, value, events and ARIA attributes target the real input. className/style customize the outer layout wrapper.
start/end are logical content slots. Adornments do not become the submitted value or an accessible label; use Field or Label and explain prefixes when needed.
The input has one shared field perimeter and accent focus. Interactive adornments keep their own focus indication and accessible names.
disabled/readOnly affect the input; host-owned addon actions need their own disabled policy. Use compatible action sizes. Text-like input types are supported; Textarea/Select are separate constructs.

name: Toggle
description: A native button with a persistent pressed state.
notes: Keep the accessible name stable; Enter/Space toggle pressed. Supports controlled pressed/onPressedChange or defaultPressed.

name: ToggleGroup
description: Optional single or multiple selections exposed as pressed buttons.
code: <ToggleGroup label="Text formatting" defaultValue={["bold"]} options={[{value: "bold", label: "Bold"}, {value: "italic", label: "Italic"}]} />
notes: Tab reaches each enabled action. Arrows/Home/End move focus without selecting. Single selection can be cleared.
Use RadioGroup for form choices and tabs for switching panels. ToggleGroup does not submit form values.

name: SegmentedControl
description: A compact single-value choice with native radio semantics and a shared inset surface.
code: <SegmentedControl label="Time range" name="period" defaultValue="day" options={[{value: "day", label: "Day"}, {value: "week", label: "Week"}, {value: "month", label: "Month"}]} />
notes: Uses original RadioGroup behavior and native inputs.
Arrow keys move focus and select; Home/End select endpoints, skipping disabled segments. Selecting the current value does not clear it.
Native name/form/required, reset and controlled values are preserved. Use actual tabs for tab panels, ToggleGroup for optional pressed actions.

name: Collapsible
description: A named disclosure button and retained show/hide panel.
notes: Use open/onOpenChange or defaultOpen. The panel stays mounted and hidden when closed; hidden form controls keep native form semantics.
Title is plain text for a stable button name. Content may be interactive. Disabled prevents trigger activation, not interaction inside an open panel.

name: Accordion
description: Related disclosure sections with optional single or multiple expansion.
code: <Accordion label="Questions" items={[{value:"install",title:"How do I install Flood?",content:"Install the packages and import the stylesheet."}]} />
notes: Headings contain native disclosure buttons. Set headingLevel for the surrounding document.
Enter/Space toggle. Tab visits available triggers and open panel contents. ArrowUp/Down and Home/End move among enabled top-level triggers without opening panels.

name: Tooltip
description: Brief text help on hover or focus, with collision-aware placement.
notes: Requires native Popover API.
Forward trigger props and ref to one actual button. Tooltip is text-only; interactive content belongs in Popover.
Escape dismisses. Hover can move onto the tooltip; focus stays on the trigger. Do not use it as the only accessible name or essential instruction.

name: Popover
description: A nonmodal contextual dialog in the native top layer.
notes: Forward all trigger props and ref.
Escape, outside pointer and focus leaving dismiss. Focus enters content and returns when appropriate; Tab is not trapped.
Closed content unmounts; keep persistent data in the host. Uses native Popover API within the existing DOM/theme scope.

name: Dialog
description: A named native modal dialog with inert background and managed focus.
code: <Dialog title="Create a project" trigger={trigger => <Button {...trigger}>Open dialog</Button>}>Project details.</Dialog>
notes: Uses native showModal, not a simulated modal div.
Escape closes the top layer; outside closing can be disabled independently. Tab remains inside the dialog.
Closed content unmounts. Forward trigger props/ref; initialFocusRef can select a safe initial control. Modern native dialog support is required.

name: Tabs
description: Connected tab buttons and retained content panels with roving keyboard focus.
notes: Arrow keys navigate enabled tabs; automatic activation is default, manual needs Enter/Space. Tab leaves the tablist. Horizontal direction follows RTL.
Inactive panels remain mounted but hidden. Keep form validation and persistent selection under host control. Invalid, missing or disabled selected values fall back to the first available item.

name: Breadcrumb
description: A wrapping hierarchy of native links with an explicit current page.
notes: The last item is current, with or without an href. Separators are decorative and not focusable.
Links keep browser navigation semantics. The host owns actual routes and client routing.

name: Pagination
description: Controlled page navigation with bounded page windows, buttons or native links.
notes: Use getHref for native route links, onPageChange for local controlled data, or both for a navigation notification. Modifier clicks retain browser behavior.
Page and pageCount must be positive safe integers within range. Empty datasets can omit Pagination. siblingCount 0/1/2 controls compactness; endpoints are noninteractive when unavailable.

name: Badge
description: A compact, noninteractive label for status and metadata.
notes: Use text to communicate status; color is supplementary.
Tone, size and visual variant are independent. This is not a selectable or removable chip.
Available in 0.2.4. Use FloodRoot for the neutral dark recipe.

name: Spinner
description: A sized loading indicator with an optional accessible status label.
notes: Standalone indicators expose a status with a localizable label. Decorative indicators are hidden from assistive technology.
Button loading uses this indicator decoratively and keeps the button name. Do not announce every spinner in a busy area.
Use Progress when completion is measurable. Reduced motion stops rotation. Available in 0.2.4.

name: Skeleton
description: A decorative placeholder that reserves space for loading content.
notes: Always hidden from assistive technology. The host owns loading announcements and aria-busy on the relevant region.
Width and height accept CSS dimensions; style overrides them. Match the final content geometry.
Animation can be disabled; reduced motion and forced colors disable the pulse. Available in 0.2.4.

name: Avatar
description: A stable identity image with initials or an explicit text fallback.
notes: Name supplies the accessible image name; decorative suppresses duplicate naming next to an equivalent visible name.
Fallback remains visible until the image loads and after a load error. Changing src starts a fresh load lifecycle.
Native span props and ref target the root. Size and shape do not change during loading. Available in 0.2.4.

name: Progress
description: Completion of a task, with a determinate or unknown value.
notes: Omit value for indeterminate progress. The accessible progressbar omits aria-valuenow in that state.
Max defaults to 100; values must be finite and inside 0..max. Invalid ranges throw instead of silently inventing a percentage.
hideLabel removes the caption visually while keeping the accessible name. valueText supplies human-readable units.
This is not a live region or a task manager. Native div props, className/style and ref target the wrapper. Available in 0.2.4.

name: Meter
description: A measured value within a meaningful, finite range.
code: <Meter label="Storage used" value={75} valueText="75 of 100 GB" />
notes: Use Meter for storage, battery or other bounded measurements; use Progress for task completion.
Value is required. Min defaults to 0 and max to 100; require min < max and min <= value <= max. Invalid values throw.
Use valueText for meaningful units; hideLabel keeps the accessible name. Tone is host-owned and does not calculate warning thresholds.
Native div props, className/style and ref target the wrapper. Available in 0.2.4.

name: Alert
description: An inline message with a quiet boundary and explicit announcement priority.
code:
<Alert tone="warning" title="Storage is almost full">
  Free some space before your next upload.
</Alert>
notes: announcement defaults off: a static message does not automatically interrupt a screen reader. Polite uses role=status; assertive uses role=alert.
Use assertive for newly inserted urgent messages, and verify with actual assistive technology. No focus movement, timeout or automatic dismissal is implemented.
Title is optional. Icons are original decorative glyphs; pass icon={null} to omit or supply noninteractive artwork. Meaning must remain in the text.
Native div props and ref target the message root. Available in 0.2.4.

name: DescriptionList
description: Related terms and descriptions with native list semantics and responsive grouping.
notes: Renders native dl/dt/dd groups. IDs are stable React keys, not generated DOM anchors; require unique nonempty IDs.
Inline layout becomes stacked when the component container is narrow. Stacked layout is always one column.
Density and dividers affect presentation. Values may contain React content; the host owns formatting and missing-value text.
Native dl props, className/style and HTMLDListElement ref target the list. Available in 0.2.4.

name: Table
description: A native data table with caption, density and a protected horizontal scroll area.
code:
ProjectMembers
Flood12
notes: Caption is required and remains the accessible table name with hideCaption. Supply table sections and correct native header/cell associations.
Native table props, className/style and HTMLTableElement ref target the actual table. Set style.minWidth when horizontal overflow is preferable to compressed columns.
Flood ScrollArea owns horizontal scrolling and keyboard access. scrollLabel can name its viewport independently; dir and hidden apply to the containing scroll area too.
Use data-numeric on headers/cells for end alignment and tabular figures; data-align=start/center/end gives logical alignment. No automatic sorting, selection, pagination or data access.
Striped and compact/comfortable density are opt-in presentation. Available in 0.2.4.

name: Menu
description: An action and preference menu with keyboard navigation and controlled checkbox/radio items.
code:
<Menu label="Project actions"
  trigger={props => <Button {...props}>Project actions</Button>}
  items={[{id:"rename",label:"Rename…"},{id:"divider",type:"separator"},{id:"delete",label:"Delete project",tone:"danger"}]}
  onAction={id => console.log(id)}
/>
notes: Forward all supplied trigger props and ref to one native button or Flood Button/IconButton. Label names the menu; action labels remain visible.
Enter/Space and ArrowDown open at the first item; ArrowUp opens at the last. Inside use arrows, Home/End and label-prefix typeahead.
Disabled items stay keyboard-focusable with aria-disabled but cannot activate. Separators are noninteractive; action IDs must be unique and nonempty. At least one action is required.
Escape closes and restores trigger focus. Tab moves to the next control after the trigger; Shift+Tab returns to the trigger. Outside interaction dismisses without stealing deliberately moved focus.

Shortcut text is a visual hint, not an implemented key binding. No href or asynchronous task manager is included. Nested items use type="submenu" and a nonempty items array. Checkbox/radio items are controlled preferences, available in 0.2.7.
Controlled open needs host updates; onAction requests closure before calling the host. Modern native Popover API required. Native div props/ref target the popup. Available in 0.2.4.

Checkbox items take checked (boolean or mixed) and onCheckedChange. Radio items take a nonempty group label, checked and onCheckedChange; the host keeps one selected item per group. Keep each radio group contiguous. Preference items stay open by default; closeOnSelect opts into dismissal. They do not call onAction or submit form values.

Submenus open by logical arrow, click/tap or cancellable mouse hover intent. Escape closes one level; Tab leaves the entire tree through the root trigger. IDs are unique across the tree and nested keyboard searches stay inside their own menu.

name: Toolbar
description: A compact action panel with one Tab entry and directional keyboard navigation.
notes: Use Button, IconButton, Toggle, native buttons/links and Menu triggers. Keep inputs, Select, Tabs and ToggleGroup outside this action-only toolbar.

Arrows move focus without activation; Home/End jump to the ends. Disabled and hidden actions are skipped. One Tab entry is established after hydration; before JavaScript native child tab order remains.
Horizontal arrows follow writing direction. Vertical arrows move between actions; open a vertical toolbar Menu with Enter/Space. Horizontal menus retain ArrowUp/Down opening.
loop defaults to true. Native div props/ref target the toolbar; preserve a meaningful label. Available in 0.2.4.
shape defaults to rounded; pill uses the action radius and a horizontal single scrollable rail.

name: Kbd
description: A quiet native keyboard-input label for keys and shortcut hints.
notes: Native kbd markup, not a button or a shortcut handler. The application implements and documents actual bindings.
Sizes sm/md/lg use relative keycap tokens. Native props/ref target the kbd element. Available in 0.2.4.

name: Card
description: A structured surface for a heading, supporting content and independent actions.
code:
<Card title="Project details" description="Release on 12 November"
  footer={<Button variant="subtle">Open project</Button>}>
  <Text as="p" size="compact">Homepage and checkout</Text>
</Card>
notes: Card composes Surface with optional title, description, header actions, children and footer. Missing slots add no empty wrapper or reserved space.
Use Surface for unstructured containment; use Card when its header/body/footer structure is useful. Card is a noninteractive div, not a button or link. Put named actions inside.
Title uses Heading at headingLevel (2 by default); choose the level according to the page. Supply phrasing content for the title. Description accepts supporting React content.
Density compact/comfortable controls padding and section rhythm using existing semantic spacing. Header actions wrap naturally; content is never clipped to the radius.
Root HTMLDivElement ref and native div props/style/className target the surface. The title prop is content, not the native HTML tooltip attribute. Available in 0.2.4.

name: Container
description: Centered content with token widths and logical gutters.
code: <Container size="md" gutter="6"><Text as="p">Content stays within a readable width.</Text></Container>
notes: Max width includes gutters (border-box). Sizes sm/md/lg use relative semantic roles; full removes the maximum.
Native div props/ref target the container. Gutter uses Space; it does not add vertical spacing or breakpoints.
Available in 0.2.4; use matching installed declarations.

name: Grid
description: An adaptive content grid with optional fixed columns.
notes: Default auto-fit columns clamp their minimum to available width, so narrow parents retain a single column.
Explicit columns retain their count; choose this deliberately. minItemWidth applies only to automatic columns and accepts a CSS length.
Cells remain ordinary content, not an ARIA grid. Use native tables for tabular relationships and host media/container queries for deliberate breakpoints.
Available in 0.2.4; use matching installed declarations.

name: VisuallyHidden
description: Nonvisual content with optional reveal when keyboard focus enters.
notes: Content remains in the accessibility tree. Default is for noninteractive text only.
Use focusable for a skip link or another focusable descendant: the wrapper becomes visible while it contains focus. Supply visible focus styling on the actual control.
This is not aria-hidden, display:none or a conditional unmount. as accepts span/div.
Available in 0.2.4; use matching installed declarations.

name: AspectRatio
description: Reserved media proportions that respond to their containing width.
notes: ratio must be finite and positive. The root reserves media geometry before image loading.
Direct img/video/iframe children fill the reserved box. Content can overflow; the component does not clip focus, menus or arbitrarily tall text.
Host media owns alt, captions, controls and loading. Native props/ref target the outer div.
Available in 0.2.4; use matching installed declarations.

name: Image
description: A native responsive image with explicit alternative text and media fitting.
code: <Image src="/flood-mark.png" alt="Flood logo" width={160} height={160} fit="contain" />
notes: alt is required; an empty string is appropriate for decorative imagery beside equivalent visible content.
Native src/srcSet/sizes/loading/decoding/dimensions, handlers and HTMLImageElement ref are preserved. Supply width/height or AspectRatio to reserve geometry.
fit cover/contain changes object-fit, not fetching, optimization or fallback behavior. Avatar composes Image with its own load/fallback lifecycle.
Available in 0.2.4; use matching installed declarations.

name: List
description: Native ordered or unordered content with token spacing and optional markers.
code:
• Install the matching packages.
  • Import the stylesheet.
  • Compose with Flood.
notes: Supply native li children. ordered chooses ol; start/reversed apply only to ordered lists. start must be a safe integer.
Hiding markers retains an explicit list role for browser/assistive-technology consistency. Content may include links or controls without changing its content-list semantics.
This is not ListBox, a selection model or a keyboard-navigation engine.
Available in 0.2.4; use matching installed declarations.

name: EmptyState
description: A quiet explanation and optional next action when content is absent.
code: <EmptyState title="No projects yet" description="Create a project to get started." actions={<Button>Create project</Button>} />
notes: Composes Stack, Heading, Text, IconSlot and Inline. Optional icon is decorative; title and description explain the missing content.
Static by default, without status/alert announcements or automatic focus. Host owns whether a result change should be announced.
Choose headingLevel for the page hierarchy. Density controls relative padding. Host actions remain ordinary named controls; no loading, fetching or error recovery engine is supplied.
Available in 0.2.4; use matching installed declarations.

name: NumberInput
description: A native numeric field with integrated decrement and increment actions.
notes: Values are finite numbers or null for an empty field. onValueChange reports edits and button/arrow steps; native min/max/step validity remains available. Out-of-bound typed values clamp on blur; a step mismatch remains native validation.
Ref and native form attributes target the input. Controlled value stays host-owned; uncontrolled form reset restores the initial value. Buttons use explicit accessible names, which can be translated.
Use Field for labels and feedback. Read-only remains selectable and prevents stepping. No currency/locale formatting or wheel interception is supplied. Available in 0.2.5.

name: Slider
description: One value or an ordered range with native keyboard controls on a shared rail.
code: <Slider label="Price range" name="price" defaultValue={[25, 75]} min={0} max={100} />
notes: value/defaultValue contain one number or an ordered pair. onValueChange returns a new array. Values snap to min-based steps and thumbs cannot cross; Tab order stays stable. Supply thumbLabels to translate or explain each handle.

Horizontal only. Direction follows the host, including RTL. Native range inputs retain keyboard behavior; pointer selection chooses the nearest handle. Names submit one or two entries; uncontrolled reset restores defaults.

hideLabel preserves the accessible legend; showValue only controls the visible numeric readout. Read-only prevents edits while keeping focus. Use hint/message/error for meaning beyond color. Touch assistive technology needs device testing. Available in 0.2.5.

name: Combobox
description: Search a defined collection and commit one option while focus stays in the input.
code:
<Field label="Framework">
  {(control) => <Combobox {...control} name="framework" options={[{value: "react", label: "React"}, {value: "vue", label: "Vue"}, {value: "svelte", label: "Svelte"}]} placeholder="Choose a framework" />}
</Field>
notes: Typing filters labels and optional keywords; labels remain presentation and only the selected option value is submitted. Enter commits the active option. Escape/Tab/outside interaction discard an uncommitted query. Emptying the input clears selection.

Native input ref, Field associations, required validity, controlled/uncontrolled value, forms/reset, read-only/disabled and IME editing are preserved. Options need unique nonempty values and labels. Disabled options remain discoverable and cannot be chosen.

Use clearable for the visible clear action; translate clearLabel/toggleLabel/listLabel/emptyMessage/invalidSelectionMessage. The popup reuses Flood ScrollArea and layer positioning. No arbitrary text, multiple selection, async fetching or virtualization engine is supplied. Available in 0.2.5.
Only the disclosure chevron is shown by default. Set clearable to opt into the extra clear-selection action; individual MultiSelect tags retain their removal buttons.

name: Tag
description: A compact label with an optional icon and a named removal action.
notes: Tag is a label, not a status Badge or a selection toggle. The host owns removal; onRemove never hides the element automatically. Use ordinary noninteractive label content.

Plain text gets a default Remove label. Rich content needs explicit removeLabel. disabled prevents removal; size and decorative icon are independent. removeButtonProps customizes the nested native action while Tag owns type, name, disabled and removal.

Standalone removal is an ordinary Tab stop. MultiSelect supplies its composite keyboard model. Geometry uses relative Flood sizing; long labels wrap and touch targets remain distinct. Available in 0.2.5.

name: MultiSelect
description: Search a collection, choose multiple values and manage them as removable tags.
notes: value/defaultValue are arrays of unique nonempty option IDs; onValueChange returns a new array. Native forms submit repeated entries with the same name, never typed query text. Uncontrolled reset restores initial values.

The shared Combobox search/layer model keeps focus in the input. Enter toggles the active option and the list stays open. Backspace in an empty input removes the last editable tag; a logical backward arrow at the start enters tag actions. Tag arrows, Delete/Backspace, Enter and Escape support keyboard editing.

Disabled selected options cannot be individually removed or cleared globally. Read-only permits copying but blocks selection and removal. Required means at least one valid selected ID. Translate removeItemLabel and the shared action/empty/validation messages.
No freeform values, remote fetching, virtualization or arbitrary tag selection engine is supplied. Available in 0.2.5.
Only the disclosure chevron is shown by default. Set clearable to opt into the extra clear-selection action; individual MultiSelect tags retain their removal buttons.

name: SearchInput
description: A native search field with a leading search icon and one clear action.
notes: Native onChange, name, form, reset, ref and Field associations are preserved. clearable defaults to true; read-only hides the clear action. Translate clearLabel. Enter keeps native form submission; filtering belongs to the host.
Composes Flood InputGroup, IconSlot and IconButton using existing semantic geometry and feedback states. Available in 0.2.5.

name: PasswordInput
description: A password field with one named visibility action.
notes: Use visible/onVisibleChange for controlled visibility or defaultVisible for an initial reveal. Translate showPasswordLabel/hidePasswordLabel. Read-only still permits inspection; disabled blocks actions. Native value/onChange, autocomplete, form and ref are preserved. Visibility does not change the value.
Composes Flood InputGroup, IconSlot and IconButton using existing semantic geometry and feedback states. Available in 0.2.5.

name: FileInput
description: A native file picker with a compact selection summary and one clear action.
code:
<Field label="Attachments" hint="Choose files from your device.">
  {control => <FileInput {...control} name="attachments" multiple />}
</Field>
notes: The browser owns FileList, native name/form/required/accept/multiple/capture behavior and the input ref. onChange retains the native event; onFilesChange receives a fresh array after selection or clear. No controlled value/defaultValue or readOnly mode is supplied.

clearable defaults to true. Localize placeholder and clearLabel. Clear restores input focus and empties the native selection; form reset clears the summary without emitting a change. Disabled includes inherited fieldset behavior. Cancelling the chooser preserves selection.

File names are shown as text, shortened visually when needed. This component only selects files; the host owns upload, progress and validation. accept is a chooser hint, not file validation. Available in 0.2.5.

Multiple selection shows a compact count and a collapsible list with full file names and localized sizes. Removing one file updates the native FileList and preserves keyboard focus; clearable=false hides both individual and global removal. Translate selectionLabel/removeFileLabel. In multiple mode, choosing again appends files. Repeated files are deduplicated by name, size, type, lastModified and relative path. Single mode replaces its selection.

name: AlertDialog
description: A focused confirmation with explicit cancel and continue actions.
code: <AlertDialog title="Archive this project?" description="You can restore it from the archive." confirmLabel="Archive project" trigger={props => <Button {...props}>Archive project</Button>} onConfirm={() => { /* Archive in the host application. */ }} />
notes: Uses the original Flood Dialog modal layer with role=alertdialog, a required message and initial focus on Cancel. Tab stays inside the modal; Escape cancels and restores trigger focus. Outside clicks do not dismiss it. There is no extra close action competing with the explicit Cancel button.

onConfirm is a host callback followed by a close request. onCancel handles the Cancel button and Escape, not confirmation. Use open/onOpenChange for host-controlled state and confirmDisabled to prevent confirmation while unavailable. Async work/errors belong to the host; callbacks are not awaited.
Translate title, description, confirmLabel and cancelLabel. Use ordinary Dialog for forms and exploratory content. Available in 0.2.5.

name: Drawer
description: A modal edge panel with a steady header, scrollable body and optional footer.
code:
<Drawer title="Project settings" description="Keep the details close." trigger={props => <Button {...props}>Open settings</Button>}>
  <Field label="Project name">{control => <Input {...control} defaultValue="Flood" />}</Field>
</Drawer>
notes: Uses Flood native Dialog focus containment, scroll lock, background inertness, nested layers and return focus. Escape and the named close IconButton dismiss it; closeOnOutsideClick defaults to true. Controlled open/onOpenChange and initialFocusRef match Dialog.

side is logical start/end or physical top/bottom. size sets 20/26/34rem for sm/md/lg, capped to the viewport. Vertical drawers occupy the viewport height; horizontal drawers occupy its width. Entry motion respects reduced motion; closing is immediate.

The body scrolls with Flood ScrollArea while the header and optional footer remain visible when space allows. Responsive padding and full-width narrow descriptions preserve the reading area at enlarged text; if the chrome cannot fit, the whole panel can scroll rather than clipping the body. Footer actions are host-owned, without implicit save or close. No swipe/drag gesture or nested navigation engine is included. Available in 0.2.5.

name: CopyButton
description: A clipboard action with stable geometry and localized result feedback.
notes: Copies only on a user click. Requires a secure context and Clipboard API; onCopyError receives unavailable/denied errors. The host owns any manual-copy fallback. Native button ref and disabled semantics are preserved.

Localize copyLabel/copiedLabel/errorLabel. resetDelay restores the idle state after success. Labels reserve their common width and a live status announces the result. No remote data transfer is built in. Available in 0.2.5.

name: ToastRegion
description: A host-controlled notification queue with timed, pausable messages and actions.
code: <ToastRegion items={[{id:"saved",title:"Changes saved",status:"success",duration:0}]} onDismiss={id => { /* Remove the item from host state. */ }} />
notes: The host owns items and removes them onDismiss. IDs must be unique/nonempty. limit controls visible items; queued timers start only when visible. Ordinary messages default to five seconds; error/action messages persist unless duration is explicit. duration=0 persists.

Timers pause on hover, focus and hidden documents. F8 focuses the first visible region without interrupting initial task focus; hotkey=false disables it. Use a single main region per document. Localize label/closeLabel and message/action text. Error messages announce as alerts; others use polite status.

placement is logical start/end. inline embeds the region in a host container; fixed mode uses ordinary document stacking, so place a contextual region inside a modal if needed. Action callbacks do not dismiss automatically. No global notification store or promise API. Available in 0.2.5.

name: AvatarGroup
description: A compact collection of avatars with an accessible overflow count.
code: <AvatarGroup label="Project collaborators" items={[{id:"alex",name:"Alex Morgan"},{id:"sam",name:"Sam Lee"},{id:"june",name:"June Park"}]} max={2} />
notes: The native list composes Flood Avatar. IDs and names must be nonempty and unique IDs remain stable. max is a positive integer; the default shows four people.

Overflow is a static count, not a hidden interactive menu. Translate overflowLabel when needed; visible avatars retain their individual accessible names. Size follows Avatar. Intentional overlap never applies to interactive targets.
Compatible addition in 0.2.5. Uses existing Flood semantic tokens and relative geometry.

name: StatusIndicator
description: A named state with a small decorative indicator, without a badge container.
notes: The visible label carries meaning; the dot is decorative and color is never the only signal. Use announce to opt into a polite status live region for changing messages.
Static labels do not announce by default. Tone is independent of wording and size. Use Badge for categorical labels and Alert for a message requiring more explanation.
Compatible addition in 0.2.5. Uses existing Flood semantic tokens and relative geometry.

name: Figure
description: A native figure that keeps media and its caption together.
notes: Composes native figure and figcaption. The host supplies the image, chart, code or other self-contained content, including its own alt text or accessible name.
captionPosition controls DOM reading order as well as placement. Caption content may contain links. Native hidden, dir, lang, style and ref target the figure.
Compatible addition in 0.2.5. Uses existing Flood semantic tokens and relative geometry.

name: Blockquote
description: A quoted passage with an optional compact attribution.
code: Good interfaces make room for what matters.
notes: Uses native blockquote; cite remains a source URL, while attribution is visible host-authored credit. Rich quote content and attribution are supported.
The logical leading rule follows RTL. Supply quotation punctuation as part of your actual content; the component does not invent a quotation or source.
Compatible addition in 0.2.5. Uses existing Flood semantic tokens and relative geometry.

name: InlineCode
description: A small monospace code fragment that participates in running text.
notes: Native code semantics, bundled monospace stack and a quiet inline surface. Content is text; no HTML parsing or syntax highlighting is performed.
wrap defaults to true for long identifiers. wrap=false preserves the fragment on one line and the host must manage overflow. Use CodeSnippet for blocks of code and Kbd for keyboard input.
Compatible addition in 0.2.5. Uses existing Flood semantic tokens and relative geometry.

name: Metric
description: A labeled value with optional contextual trend and supporting text.
code: <Metric label="Monthly revenue" value="$24,580" trend={{direction:"up",label:"12.8% higher",tone:"success"}} hint="Compared with the previous month." />
notes: Native definition-list semantics associate the label with its value, trend and hint. Values may be rich content; the host owns currency, number and locale formatting.

Trend direction and semantic tone are independent: a decreasing failure rate can be good. Its label must communicate the change without relying on the decorative arrow or color. No automatic percentage calculation is performed.
Compatible addition in 0.2.5. Uses existing Flood semantic tokens and relative geometry.

name: Timeline
description: An ordered sequence of events with state, context and optional time labels.
notes: The native ordered list is read in the supplied order; the component does not sort or group events. IDs/titles are nonempty, IDs are unique and at most one event may be current.
Each state has a visually hidden text equivalent; localize stateLabels. timeLabel is user-facing text and dateTime, when supplied, is the machine-readable time. Both are host-owned.
Markers and optional artwork are decorative. This is an event display, not a wizard or navigation control. Long descriptions and times wrap without changing marker alignment.
Compatible addition in 0.2.5. Uses existing Flood semantic tokens and relative geometry.

name: NavigationList
description: A grouped list of native navigation links with a clear current destination.
notes: NavigationList renders nav, lists and native anchors; it is not an ARIA menu or tablist. The host supplies unique stable item values, destinations and currentValue. Browser modifier/target navigation is preserved through item.linkProps.

Optional group names label contiguous item groups. Icons are decorative IconSlot content; descriptions remain associated link text. Size controls compact row density while coarse pointer targets remain usable. No routing engine, URL inference or disabled navigation simulation is supplied.
Original compatible addition in the unpublished 0.2.5 source candidate.

name: Steps
description: An ordered progress sequence with explicit current, completed, upcoming and error states.
notes: Steps renders an ordered list, not tabs. currentValue identifies aria-current=step; preceding steps default to complete and later steps to upcoming. Item status may explicitly mark complete/upcoming/error. Omitted currentValue starts at the first step.

Without onStepChange, steps are informative content. Providing it renders native step buttons; the host owns navigation and currentValue updates. Disabled items only affect those actions. Every state has text through customizable statusLabels; color and icons are additional cues. Horizontal presentation stacks in narrow viewports.
Original compatible addition in the unpublished 0.2.5 source candidate.

name: Section
description: A named document section with a compact heading, supporting description and optional actions.
code:
<Section title="Project settings" description="Manage details your team shares." headingLevel={2}>
  <Text as="p">Section content.</Text>
</Section>
notes: Section renders a native section and heading. A generated heading ID labels the region; explicit id creates a deterministic heading ID. headingLevel follows the host document hierarchy.

The title and description share a close text column; actions align separately and wrap when necessary. It adds no surface or border. Compose Surface or another container inside when content needs its own background.
Original compatible addition in the unpublished 0.2.5 source candidate.
headingLevel chooses h2–h6 for the document outline; it does not set the visual scale. headingSize independently selects the existing Heading typography role (section by default).

name: Split
description: A responsive main-and-supporting layout with logical pane placement and container-based collapse.
code: <Split side="end" ratio="main" collapseAt="md" main={<Text as="p">Main content</Text>} aside={<Text as="p">Supporting content</Text>} />
notes: main and aside are content slots in generic div panes; they do not introduce duplicate main landmarks. side places the supporting pane at logical start/end and preserves the same DOM reading order. ratio chooses equal panes or a 2:1 emphasis on main/aside.

Container queries collapse at sm=30rem, md=48rem or lg=64rem; never retains two columns. gap uses the spacing scale. This is layout composition, with no resizing gesture, saved pane sizes or splitter keyboard model.
Original compatible addition in the unpublished 0.2.5 source candidate.

name: Center
description: Center a constrained piece of content in both axes of an available region.
notes: Center supplies two-axis alignment with an inner content wrapper. minHeight sets the available vertical region; maxWidth constrains the content rather than the entire parent. Values are ordinary CSS lengths, preferably rem.

inline opts into inline-grid for centering within text or an inline composition. It adds no content semantics, surface, spacing between siblings or viewport positioning. Use Stack/Inline for collections and Container for page gutters.
Original compatible addition in the unpublished 0.2.5 source candidate.

name: SkipLink
description: A native skip-navigation link revealed on focus and aimed at a page content target.
notes: Place SkipLink early in DOM order and point href at a nonempty same-page fragment. The target should have tabIndex=-1 (or already be focusable). Native fragment navigation updates the URL; the component then focuses and reveals the target.

It stays visually hidden until focused. The click handler respects prevented events, modifier navigation and new-window targets. Reduced motion uses immediate scrolling. It does not create a focus trap or change the target tabindex.
Original compatible addition in the unpublished 0.2.5 source candidate.

name: ListBox
description: A named single or multiple selection list with native validation and semantic feedback.
notes: Use a scalar value/defaultValue in single mode and an array in multiple mode. onValueChange returns the matching shape. Stable, unique nonempty option IDs are submitted as repeated hidden native form fields when name is supplied. Uncontrolled reset restores the initial selection.

The list owns one Tab stop and aria-activedescendant. Arrows/Home/End move through enabled options; single selection follows navigation. Space/Enter selects or toggles. Typing searches option-label prefixes. Disabled options cannot be selected; readOnly retains navigation and copying without changing the value.

Provide a clear label or use hideLabel with the accessible label preserved. Use disabled on the composite to remove its Tab stop. The list is not virtualized and does not fetch options. Available in 0.2.5.
required validates accepted selection; readonly bypasses validation and disabled excludes form values.
description/message and status share the field feedback contract. validationMessage is a host-owned blocking constraint.

name: PinInput
description: One native code editor presented as a compact row of character slots.
code: <PinInput label="Verification code" name="code" length={6} autoComplete="one-time-code" required />
notes: One real native input preserves mobile one-time-code autofill, clipboard, selection, forms and required validity; decorative slots are hidden from assistive technology. Use its native ref for focus. The host owns verification and authentication.

length is an integer from 1 to 12. mode numeric permits ASCII digits; alphanumeric also permits ASCII letters. Paste strips separators and invalid characters, then respects the selection and length. Backspace and arrow editing remain native. Use mask to visually conceal the code.

Use value/onValueChange or defaultValue. Native form reset restores the initial uncontrolled value. Pattern validity requires a complete code when nonempty; required also rejects an empty code. Translate label and preserve its accessible name with hideLabel. Available in 0.2.5.

name: Rating
description: A compact star rating backed by a named native radio group.
notes: Provide a nonempty name for native radio grouping and form submission. value/defaultValue are integers from zero (unselected) to max; max is an integer from 1 to 10. Uncontrolled native reset restores defaultValue. required uses native group validation.

Arrow keys follow logical direction, Home/End jump to the first/last value, and Space selects the focused radio. One radio is in Tab order. readOnly keeps the current selection focusable without allowing changes; disabled is native.

Use getValueLabel to localize each radio name. The stars are decorative; native named radios carry the value. hideLabel preserves the legend for assistive technology. No fractional values or review submission engine is included. Available in 0.2.5.

name: Dropzone
description: A file drop target composed with the native Flood FileInput.
notes: The existing FileInput remains the real chooser and successful native form control. Dropping files dispatches the same selection flow: multiple appends and deduplicates; single selection keeps the first dropped file. Native form reset and per-file removal remain intact.

The zone responds only to file drags and prevents navigation on file drop. Disabled fields reject drops. Translate label/description and FileInput action labels. The chooser remains keyboard accessible; dropping is an additional pointer workflow.

accept guides the native chooser; the host must validate dropped file types, size and contents. Directories, remote transfer, progress, server upload and image processing are outside this control. No file contents are read. Available in 0.2.5.

name: CharacterCount
description: Supporting character or remaining-length feedback with an explicit over-limit message.
code: <CharacterCount value="Make room for a clear idea." max={80} htmlFor="project-note" />
notes: Pass text through value or supply an explicit nonnegative integer count for a host-defined counting rule. The default text count uses Unicode code points, not UTF-16 code units or grapheme clusters. max is advisory and does not truncate or validate an editor.

mode remaining displays max minus count; count displays the current count and optional limit. An over-limit message is visible in addition to its semantic color. Translate label/overLimitLabel; lang formats the number.

Use htmlFor to associate supporting output with its editor and aria-describedby on the editor when appropriate. Live announcements default off to avoid announcing every keystroke; the host may opt into aria-live. Available in 0.2.5.

name: Editable
description: Inline editing with explicit save/cancel and a committed form value.
notes: Preview and edit modes keep a separate draft. Enter commits and Escape cancels; IME composition does not submit.
Use blurAction to commit, cancel or preserve the draft on outside focus. Moving focus to the save/cancel actions is internal to the editor.
The host owns controlled value and editing props; callbacks request changes. The hidden named form field contains only the committed value.
readOnly keeps a copyable field; disabled prevents editing. Localized action labels and inputRef are available. Introduced in 0.2.7.

name: TagInput
description: Free-form text tokens with keyboard entry, removal and named form values.
code: <TagInput label="Topics" defaultValue={["Design", "React"]} name="topics" placeholder="Add a topic…" />
notes: Use TagInput for values the user may create. Use MultiSelect for a fixed option collection.
Enter and configured delimiters commit trimmed, unique tags. Pasting separated text adds multiple tags. IME composition is preserved.
Each committed tag submits one entry under name. required applies to committed tags; a draft is not a submitted token. Form reset preserves controlled ownership.
Backspace on an empty draft removes the last token. Read only preserves copying and form values; disabled omits submission and removal. Introduced in 0.2.7.

name: CommandList
description: Search and invoke commands with grouped results and keyboard navigation.
code: <CommandList label="Search commands" items={[{id:"new",label:"New project",group:"Projects"},{id:"settings",label:"Open settings",group:"Workspace"}]} onAction={id => console.log(id)} />
notes: CommandList invokes actions; Combobox and MultiSelect edit form values. A command list has no submitted name or persistent selected value.
Typing filters labels, descriptions, group names and keywords. Arrow keys, Home/End and Enter navigate and invoke enabled commands. Escape remains available to a host Dialog.
Use query/onQueryChange for host ownership or defaultQuery for local filtering. Loading blocks stale invocation and exposes an announcement; the host owns asynchronous work and cancellation.

The ref targets the native search input. Native div props target the wrapper. Translate labels, placeholder, emptyMessage and loadingMessage; hideLabel preserves the search name. No modal, global shortcut or router integration is implied. Introduced in 0.2.7.

name: DateField
description: Segmented Gregorian date entry with canonical form values and explicit date validation.
notes: Uses three native text segments rather than an operating-system calendar popup. Calendar and DatePicker are separate contracts.
Values are canonical YYYY-MM-DD dates from 0001 through 9999, or an empty string. min/max and leap years use civil date arithmetic without timezones.
Arrow keys adjust segments. Left/Right move at segment boundaries; IME and modifier shortcuts remain available. Use explicit order and localized segmentLabels/messages.
In editable fields, incomplete or invalid drafts block native submission; the hidden named field contains no stale previous date. Controlled values and form resets preserve host ownership.

Read only retains copying and accepted canonical submission, even outside current bounds or application constraints. It bypasses native validity without accepting partial or refused drafts. Disabled fields and fieldsets remain excluded. Introduced in the unpublished 0.2.7 source candidate.

name: TimeField
description: Segmented 24-hour time entry with canonical values, bounds and a seconds-based step.
notes: Use HH:mm with minute precision or HH:mm:ss with second precision. Values have no date or timezone.
step is expressed in seconds and anchored to min or midnight; minute precision requires a multiple of 60. Overnight ranges are not inferred.

In editable fields, incomplete, invalid, out-of-range, step-mismatched and refused controlled drafts block native submission. Readonly preserves accepted canonical time outside bounds/step alignment; it never accepts a partial or refused draft. Disabled values are excluded.
Click the control background to focus a missing or remembered segment. Keyboard steps, Home/End, paste and IME preserve host cancellation. Translate segmentLabels and messages. Introduced in 0.2.7.

name: Calendar
description: One calendar with day, month and year views, without nested popups.
code: <Calendar label="Choose a date" defaultValue="2026-10-26" today="2026-10-26" weekStartsOn={1} />
notes: Calendar is a standalone visual collection. DateField handles text entry and DatePicker composes the field and calendar layer.
Values use canonical YYYY-MM-DD and visibleMonth uses YYYY-MM. Locale formats Gregorian month/day names; weekStartsOn is explicit.
Arrows move dates; Home/End move within a week and PageUp/PageDown navigate months. Controlled month refusal preserves a real focused day. Disabled dates remain discoverable but cannot select.

The host owns selected values, availability and side effects. Provide today for a deterministic clock in tests or rendering. Min/max bound navigation; readonly prevents selection while allowing browsing. Introduced in 0.2.7.
Month and year controls replace the content of this calendar. Selecting a navigation period returns to days without changing the selected date.
granularity="day" | "month" | "year" chooses YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM or YYYY.

name: DatePicker
description: A segmented date field with an integrated calendar picker and shared form value.
notes: Composes Flood DateField, Calendar and Popover; text input and visual selection share one canonical value and form bridge.
Activate the calendar icon or Alt+ArrowDown in a segment. Escape/outside dismissal returns or preserves intended focus through the existing overlay engine. Selecting a day closes the calendar.
Read only and disabled prevent opening or date changes; native disabled fieldsets remain inert. Invalid/incomplete drafts retain native DateField validation.

Controlled value and open state are independently host-owned. Native form reset restores the initial uncontrolled date and preserves cancelled resets. Translate calendarLabel/openCalendarLabel, month navigation, segment labels and messages.
DateField remains the keyboard-entry primitive; Calendar remains independently usable. Introduced in the unpublished 0.2.7 source candidate.

name: ErrorSummary
description: A linked validation summary that focuses host-owned invalid fields.
code: <ErrorSummary title="Review the form" errors={[{id:"project",fieldId:"project",message:"Enter a project name."}]} />
notes: The host supplies errors; ErrorSummary does not infer validation or submit a form. Each entry links to an exact field ID.
Normal activation focuses the target while modifier navigation remains native. onSelect can cancel the action before focus moves.
announcement defaults to off. autoFocus opts into focus on appearance, not on every error update, and suppresses duplicate live announcements. Empty errors render nothing. Introduced in 0.2.7.

name: ResizablePanels
description: Two panels separated by an accessible pointer and keyboard resize control.
notes: Percentages describe the main pane and exclude the dedicated separator track. The host supplies content and scrolling.
Drag the separator or use logical arrow keys, Home/End and Shift for large steps. Horizontal resizing follows RTL direction.
value/onValueChange keeps the host in control. onValueCommit reports an accepted completed interaction; pointer cancellation restores the initial uncontrolled size.
The separator occupies space so its touch area does not overlap panel content. Persisting layout and larger panel graphs belong to the host. Introduced in 0.2.7.

name: RangeCalendar
description: A Gregorian grid for selecting and previewing one continuous date interval.
notes: The first activation chooses a start; the second completes a normalized ordered interval. Hover and focus can preview an unfinished interval without committing.
Controlled values include partial {start,end:""}; the host must accept that partial value to advance selection. onRangeSelect confirms an enabled completed interval.
isDateDisabled controls endpoints. isRangeDisabled validates the entire interval; interior blocked dates are not inferred by scanning arbitrary date spans.
Reuses the Calendar grid, month navigation, focus and localization contracts. Translate rangeLabels for instruction messages. Introduced in 0.2.7.

name: DateRangeField
description: Two segmented date fields with one ordered range and atomic form values.
notes: The value is {start,end}, with canonical YYYY-MM-DD dates or empty endpoints. Editable partial, reversed, unavailable and refused ranges block native submission. Readonly submits a complete ordered accepted pair despite current bounds/availability; partial, reversed and refused pairs stay atomic empty values.
Both named bridges represent one range contract. The group owns relationship validation while each DateField preserves its calendar validity and keyboard behavior.
Start/end names and labels are explicit; min/max, readonly/disabled, status and form reset follow the field contracts.
Use DateRangePicker for visual interval selection. Introduced in 0.2.7.

name: DateRangePicker
description: Paired date entry with one calendar popup for continuous interval selection.
notes: Composes DateRangeField, RangeCalendar and the existing Popover engine. One popup selects start and end; it closes after an enabled complete interval.
The popup follows the whole fields region width and clamps to the viewport. Text and calendar editing share the same partial/complete range contract.
Controlled range/open state and availability remain host-owned. Escape/outside dismissal does not turn an incomplete range into a valid submission.
Translate endpoint, calendar and range instruction labels. Introduced in 0.2.7.

name: ContextMenu
description: Context actions at the pointer or keyboard target, sharing the Menu interaction engine.
code: <ContextMenu label="Project actions" items={[{id:"rename",label:"Rename"},{id:"duplicate",label:"Duplicate"}]} onAction={id => console.log(id)}><Surface padding="6">Right-click or use Shift+F10.</Surface></ContextMenu>
notes: Right click opens at the pointer; ContextMenu or Shift+F10 opens near the actual focused target. The wrapper is keyboard-focusable and named.
Uses the same Menu items, preferences, nested layers, typeahead and keyboard navigation. Leaf commands close the tree; Escape unwinds one level and restores the real source focus.
disabled preserves the native browser context menu. Controlled open and onAction remain host-owned. Provide a visible Menu action as a primary alternative on touch devices. Introduced in 0.2.7.

name: Tree
description: A selectable application hierarchy with independent expansion and keyboard focus.
notes: Tree uses tree/treeitem/group semantics, logical arrows, Home/End and typeahead. Moving focus does not select an item. Enter/Space explicitly selects; multiple selection does not cascade.

Items have globally unique values. Expansion uses expandedValues/defaultExpandedValues/onExpandedValuesChange; selection uses value/defaultValue/onValueChange. Controlled refusal preserves the host state.

Read-only allows browsing without selecting. Disabled items remain discoverable but cannot select or expand. hasChildren/loading represent host-owned deferred branches; no fetching or virtualization is built in.
Application selection writes no form values. Use NavigationTree for ordinary native links. Introduced in 0.2.7.

name: NavigationTree
description: Nested native navigation links with separate disclosure controls.
notes: Native nav, lists and anchors preserve ordinary Tab order and browser modifier navigation. This component does not use ARIA tree/menu/tab roles.

A branch may have both href and children: its native link navigates while a separate disclosure button expands. currentValue marks the matching destination; ancestors are expanded explicitly by the host.

Expansion is controlled or uncontrolled through expandedValues/defaultExpandedValues/onExpandedValuesChange. Translate disclosure names with expandLabel; content can render host-owned loading or empty branch content.
Item values must be globally unique and children acyclic. Disabled destinations have no active href; parent disability does not propagate to children. Introduced in 0.2.7.

name: ColorSwatch
description: A named sample of an opaque RGB color.
notes: Opaque RGB colors only; keep a text label wherever color conveys meaning.

name: ColorPicker
description: An RGB color editor with hex input, channel sliders and reusable presets.
notes: Uses #rrggbb values without alpha or gradients.
The hex field owns native form validation; RGB controls provide an additional editing path.

name: HoverCard
description: A focusable preview that opens on hover, keyboard focus or explicit activation.
code:
<HoverCard title="Alex Morgan" trigger={props => <Button {...props} variant="subtle">Alex Morgan</Button>}>
  <Text as="p" size="compact">Designer at Flood.</Text>
  <Link href="https://github.com/tillwithered">View profile</Link>
</HoverCard>
notes: Interactive content belongs to a named dialog preview, not a tooltip.
Click pins the preview; keyboard and touch users can activate the trigger.

name: TreeSelect
description: Single selection from a hierarchical collection inside a popup.
notes: This first version selects one item; Tree provides standalone multiple selection.
Values are globally unique and expansion remains independent of selection.

name: DateTimePicker
description: A composed civil date and wall-clock time with separate form values.
notes: Date and time submit as separate fields. No timezone, UTC conversion or instant is inferred.
Date bounds and daily time bounds are independent. Use application validation for cross-field business rules.

name: DataList
description: A native list of structured rows with independent links and actions.
code:
<DataList>
  <DataListItem title="Design system" description="Foundations and components" metadata="Updated today" />
  <DataListItem title="Website" description="Documentation and examples" metadata="Updated yesterday" />
</DataList>
notes: This is a ul/li list, not a listbox or data grid.
Keep navigation in the title link and actions in their own buttons.

name: DataListItem
description: A structured list row with media, supporting text, metadata and actions.
code:
<DataList>
  <DataListItem title="Design system" description="Foundations and components" metadata="Updated today" />
</DataList>
notes: Render inside DataList or another native list.
The row is not clickable; supply a Link as title when navigation is needed.

name: CheckCard
description: A native checkbox presented as a selectable content card.
code: <CheckCard label="Product updates" description="A monthly summary of new features." name="updates" value="product" />
notes: Uses native checkbox semantics, including mixed state, required and form reset.
Content is noninteractive: do not nest links or actions inside a card label.

name: RadioCard
description: A native radio choice presented as a selectable content card.
code:
<Fieldset legend="Plan">
  <Stack gap="2">
    <RadioCard name="plan" value="starter" label="Starter" description="1 project, up to 3 members" metadata="Free" defaultChecked />
    <RadioCard name="plan" value="team" label="Team" description="Unlimited projects, up to 25 members" metadata="$12 / month" />
  </Stack>
</Fieldset>
notes: Group choices in a Fieldset and give them the same name.
Native arrow-key behavior, forms and reset remain available. Apply readOnly consistently to the whole group.

name: DataTable
description: A native data table with local sorting, page-scoped selection and pagination.
code:
<DataTable caption="Projects" selectable pageSize={5}
  columns={[{id:"name",label:"Project",sortable:true},{id:"status",label:"Status"}]}
  rows={[{id:"design",label:"Design system",cells:{name:"Design system",status:"Active"}}]} />
notes: Supply the complete client collection; remote/server pagination and virtualization are not part of this API.
Select all affects selectable rows on the current page and preserves selection on other pages.
Use sortValues for rich React cells; missing values sort last in both directions.

name: FileItem
description: A named file row with size, type, thumbnail and independent actions.
notes: Render inside FileList or another native list.
No file reading, object URL creation or uploading is performed.

name: FileList
description: A named native list of file rows.
code:
<FileList label="Attachments">
  <FileItem name="Brand guidelines.pdf" size={2400000} mimeType="PDF" />
  <FileItem name="Logo.svg" size={18400} mimeType="SVG" />
</FileList>
notes: List contents and file identities are host owned. Narrow list containers adapt media, copy and actions without hiding primitive anatomy, including on a wide screen.
Use stable host IDs for React keys; a name is not a unique file identity.

name: UploadItem
description: A host-controlled upload row with explicit progress and applicable actions.
code:
<UploadList label="Uploads">
  <UploadItem name="Brand guidelines.pdf" size={2400000} state="uploading" progress={45} />
</UploadList>
notes: Queued/uploading can expose cancel; error/cancelled can expose retry; settled rows can expose remove.
Unknown progress is indeterminate. StatusIndicator and Progress remain distinct reused primitives; their row can wrap when the list container is constrained. No network or upload queue is built in.

name: UploadList
description: A named native list of host-controlled upload rows.
code:
<UploadList label="Uploads">
  <UploadItem name="Brand guidelines.pdf" state="uploading" progress={45} />
  <UploadItem name="Logo.svg" state="success" />
  <UploadItem name="Cover.png" state="error" error="Connection interrupted" />
</UploadList>
notes: Each row has its own state and stable host identity.
Cancellation, retry and removal callbacks are intents for the application.

name: ImagePreview
description: A single-image preview in Flood Dialog with loading and failure feedback.
code:
<ImagePreview title="Flood mark" src="/flood-mark.png" alt="Pink Flood mark"
  trigger={props => <Button {...props} variant="subtle">Preview image</Button>} />
notes: Loads the image only while its dialog content is mounted.
The host owns trusted URLs, object URL lifetime and download permissions.

name: FileMeta
description: A compact combined file-format and byte-size chip.
notes: The format label is display metadata, not validated MIME detection.
Size uses SI units; formatSize customizes the text. Missing values do not create empty chip slots. Long metadata may wrap inside its single Badge at enlarged or constrained widths.

name: TimePicker
description: A segmented time field with an anchored, keyboard-accessible list of clock times.
code: <TimePicker label="Start time" name="time" defaultValue="09:30" min="08:00" max="18:00" interval={1800} />
notes: Interval and step use seconds; the list contains at most 1000 entries.
Manual entry remains available; this is wall-clock time without timezone conversion.
One flat list, with selected-time visibility and a trailing action aligned with DatePicker.

name: DateTimeRangePicker
description: An ordered civil date/time range with four atomic form values.
code:
<DateTimeRangePicker label="Booking" startDateName="startDate" startTimeName="startTime" endDateName="endDate" endTimeName="endTime"
  defaultValue={{start:{date:"2026-10-27",time:"09:00"},end:{date:"2026-10-27",time:"18:00"}}} required />
notes: Incomplete and reversed ranges do not contribute accepted values.
No timezone or timestamp inference. Server availability remains host owned.
Only range and endpoint headings are visible; individual field names remain accessible.

name: Autocomplete
description: A free text field with optional suggestions; accepts values outside the list.
notes: The submitted value is text, not an option ID. Use Combobox for fixed choices.
Manual suggestions use controlled value and optionsQuery; stale results cannot be chosen. Network ownership remains with the host.

name: OverflowActions
description: A priority-based action row that moves commands into a More menu when space is limited.
notes: Compose commands rather than links. Higher priority remains visible longer; source order is preserved.
Uses existing Toolbar, Button, IconSlot and Menu; hidden measurements are inert and excluded from the accessibility tree.
shape defaults to pill; rounded restores the field-radius Toolbar shell. Available width excludes Toolbar padding.

name: Menubar
description: Coordinated desktop application command menus with roving triggers and shared open state.
notes: Arrow keys coordinate enabled menu triggers; child menus reuse Menu focus and dismissal.
Use native links and NavigationList for destinations, not Menubar. Controlled openValue may refuse transitions.
